text_blocks.snippet: The Rayquaza Gold Star (Card #107/107) from the 2005 Pokémon TCG expansion EX Deoxys is one of the most iconic and valuable vintage Pokémon cards in existence.

list.snippet: Rarity: Ultra Rare (Gold Star variant, featuring Rayquaza's black/shiny form)
Spiral Rush (30x): Flips a coin until tails; does 30 damage times the number of heads.
Holy Star (100): Discards all Energy cards attached to Rayquaza Star and deals 100 damage to each of the opponent's Pokémon-ex.
Holy Star (100): Discards all Energy cards attached to Rayquaza Star and deals 100 damage to each of the opponent's Pokémon-ex.
Historical Significance: It was the first Shining/Gold Star Rayquaza card ever printed. You can inspect official card details on TCGplayer.

text_blocks.snippet: Prices vary drastically depending on the card's condition and grading authority:

list.snippet: Ungraded / Raw: Typically ranges from several thousand to over $7,000 depending on wear.

Graded Copies (PSA / CGC / BGS): Mid-tier grades (like PSA 4–7) trade between $12,000 and $55,000, while high grades (PSA 9 to PSA 10) range from roughly $63,000 to over $365,000. Track live market changes and historical sales via PriceCharting.
Record Sales: A historic milestone was reached when a rare CGC Pristine 10 copy sold at auction through Fanatics Collect for $1,020,000, making it one of the most expensive Pokémon cards ever sold.
Low Print/Open Volume: The EX Deoxys set had a smaller print run compared to modern sets.
Tough Pull Rates: Gold Star cards in the EX era were pulled roughly once every 100 packs (about one per box display).

Condition Issues: The set is notoriously prone to factory edge wear and silvering/peeling around the foil borders, making high-grade copies (PSA 10 or CGC Pristine 10) extraordinarily scarce. You can browse active listings on platforms like eBay.
